خَسِيسٌ , applied to a man, and to a lot or portion or share, (S, A, K,) or a thing, (Msb, TA,) Low or ignoble, base, vile, mean or sordid, weak; (S, A, K;) [or, more commonly,] contemptible; (A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ مُسْتَخِسٌّ and ↓ مُسْتَخَسٌّ ; (K;) and, applied to a thing, also, paltry, or inconsiderable; and so ↓ خُسَاسٌ and ↓ مَخْسُوسٌ ; bad, corrupt, abominable, or disapproved: (TA:) fem. with ة: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. masc. أَخِسَّآءُ and خِسَاسٌ (Msb, TA) and أَخِسَّةٌ; (A;) pl. fem. خَسَائِسُ. (Mgh, Msb.) ―
-b2- حَظٌّ خَسِيسٌ, and ↓ مَخْسُوسٌ , (tropical:) A low, or mean, fortune, that is not held in any estimation. (A.) ―
-b3- هُوَ لَا يَدْخُلُ فِى خِسَاسِ الأُمُورِ (tropical:) [He will not enter into low, mean, or contemptible, affairs]. (A.) ―
-b4- خَسِيسٌ is also applied to A disbeliever, an unbeliever, or infidel. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
